title: Tessera disk rescue: research frontier
subtitle: A compact page for the two choices still open.
summary: The corpus now has 5,337 unique URLs across 34 inputs. It includes 3,005 non-automated behavior records, 1,788 automated GitHub candidates, 30 Apple system facts, 426 owner or implementation facts, and 88 market signals. Only recovery behavior and post-failure behavior need your choice. No files were changed.

sections.title: What the new records say
sections.intro: The latest issues repeat one point: storage roles depend on the owner and the current state.

items: Games mix redownloadable payloads with saves, mods, launcher registration, external paths, partial downloads, and runtime state.
Package stores mix shared dependencies with local sources, locks, offline rebuild needs, and project materializations.
Profiles mix caches with sessions, databases, drafts, encryption, offline data, and account recovery state.
Communication stores mix attachments with exports, linked devices, encryption, sync, local databases, and active writers.
These are discovery cases, not permission to add a broad deletion rule.

sections.title: Current product boundary
sections.intro: The study has 34 patterns. These three rules now control the next implementation decision.

rows: Store identity and coverage. Invalidate changed scope. Re-check path, volume, type, owner, lock, sync, and capacity before staging and action.
A communication root is mixed state
Protect the root until an owner action proves exact scope, active-writer state, recovery path, and remote effect.
Path and name are not enough
The current safeRegenerable classifier must not drive a safe label until the shared identity and owner-state gate exists.

sections.title: Round 7: choose recovery behavior
sections.intro: Backups, snapshots, Docker images, and VM bundles have restore value and owner-controlled state.

blocks.title: Choose the recovery boundary
blocks.description: The recommended choices protect recovery objects while showing the exact owner action and measured state.

fields.label: 1. What should Tessera do with backups and VM bundles?
fields.description: A large bundle may be a current restore path, an old device backup, a live environment, or an owner-managed disk image.

options.label: Owner app only
options.description: Keep device backups, Time Machine, Docker, Parallels, UTM, and similar bundles protected; show the exact owner next step.

options.label: Review raw path
options.description: Show the exact path, state, and a strong warning; allow inspection without placing it in safe staging.

fields.label: 2. What proof should be required before reclaim?
fields.description: A Trash move cannot recreate a lost restore point, guest state, or persistent volume.

options.label: Require verified copy
options.description: Require a verified backup or restore point and show when it was last checked before a source-aware reclaim.

options.label: Warn and review
options.description: Show the missing proof and let the user continue to a review step after a stronger warning.

fields.label: 3. What evidence should a disk-image row show?
fields.description: Host file size, physical allocation, guest capacity, snapshots, and runtime state can disagree.

options.label: Host, guest, and runtime
options.description: Show logical and physical size, guest or runtime state, snapshots, owner, and restore role when known.

options.label: Host file only
options.description: Keep the row compact and show only the host file size until the user opens details.

fields.label: Your notes
fields.description: Name a backup, VM, snapshot, owner app, or restore boundary that must shape the first version.
fields.placeholder: For example: never delete a Time Machine or Docker bundle; show me the owner action and last verified restore point.

sections.title: Round 10: choose failure behavior
sections.intro: A failed cleanup, backup, update, copy, or sync attempt can change the state or block the next safe step.

blocks.title: Choose the post-failure boundary
blocks.description: The recommended choices keep a failed case inspectable and prevent a silent retry or a wider delete batch.

fields.label: 1. What should Tessera do after a failed transaction?
fields.description: The failure may have changed the path, owner state, sync state, or usable space.

options.label: Pause and inspect
options.description: Save the exact scope and error, re-measure, and ask before retrying or changing the plan.

options.label: Retry same plan
options.description: Try the same operation again when the failure looks temporary, while keeping the existing confirmation.

fields.label: 2. How should Tessera explain the blocker?
fields.description: The next safe step depends on whether the cause is measurement, permission, sync, backup, or an owner app.

options.label: Show blocker and owner
options.description: Name the failed transaction, exact blocker, measured state, responsible owner, and one safe next step.

options.label: One generic next step
options.description: Keep the result short and suggest one broad action such as rescan, restart, or try again.

fields.label: 3. Should Tessera do work in the background after failure?
fields.description: Users report losing trust when a cleanup or sync action continues without a clear visible state.

options.label: No background work
options.description: Stop mutation and monitoring after the result unless the user starts an explicit, local observer.

options.label: Allow quiet observer
options.description: Keep a local, read-only observer running to report whether space or owner state changes.

fields.label: Your notes
fields.description: Tell me what Tessera should show or save when the first cleanup, backup, update, copy, or sync step fails.
fields.placeholder: For example: stop, explain the exact blocker, save the case, and never try a wider delete without asking.

items: Consume the two answers and update the decision ledger. Keep answered choices read-only on the next page.
Manually code the 1,788 GitHub candidates. Record false positives, duplicate behavior, maintainer-only text, and platform mismatch.
Resume page 5 after the API reset or with authenticated access.
Collect direct owner documentation and user reports for communication storage before adding an adapter.
After implementation starts, re-scan the real macOS path and test the full user flow again.
